title: Fakr ad-Din mosque built
description: The first sultan of Mogadishu builds the Fakr ad-Din mosque, one of the oldest monuments of the city-states that run the coast's trade with Arabia and India.

title: Fall of Sa'ad ad-Din
description: Emperor Yeshaq of Ethiopia captures and kills King Sa'ad ad-Din II at Zeila; the surviving Walashma princes re-form their sultanate as Adal from exile in Yemen.

title: Battle of Barawa
description: A fleet under Tristão da Cunha and Afonso de Albuquerque sacks the wealthy port of Barawa but cannot hold it.

title: British protectorate
description: Britain, supplying its garrison at Aden, signs protection treaties with the northern clans and takes over the coast as Egypt pulls out of the Sudan.

title: Italian protectorates
description: The Majeerteen and Hobyo sultans sign protection treaties with Italy, which pieces together Italian Somaliland on the centre and south coast.

title: Dervish movement
description: The preacher Mohammed Abdullah Hassan takes up arms against the British, beginning a fierce twenty-year resistance.

title: Battle of Dul Madoba
description: The Dervishes shatter the British Camel Constabulary and kill its commander Richard Corfield, one of their greatest victories.

title: Dervishes defeated
description: Bombers of the Royal Air Force pound the Dervish forts at Taleh and the movement collapses; the Sayyid dies of influenza within the year.

title: Italian conquest
description: After beating the imperial defenders at Tug Argan, Italian forces take Berbera and the whole of British Somaliland, their only lasting conquest of the war.

title: Somali Youth League founded
description: Thirteen young men found the club that becomes the Somali Youth League, the movement that leads the country to independence.

title: Italian trusteeship
description: The former Italian colony goes back to Italy for a ten-year UN trusteeship with independence promised at the end.

title: State of Somaliland
description: British Somaliland becomes the independent State of Somaliland, recognised for five days before its planned union.

title: Union and independence
description: The State of Somaliland unites with the Trust Territory of Somalia to form the Somali Republic under a civilian government.

title: Siad Barre coup
description: Major General Siad Barre seizes power days after the president's murder and sets up a socialist military state.

title: Latin alphabet adopted
description: The government standardises a Latin alphabet for Somali, launching mass literacy campaigns.

title: SNM founded
description: Isaaq exiles in London found the Somali National Movement, the first big armed opposition to Barre.

title: Hargeisa bombings
description: The air force bombs and artillery level Hargeisa and Burao after the SNM offensive, the turning point that breaks the regime in the north.

title: Siad Barre falls
description: Rebels drive Siad Barre out of Mogadishu; the state collapses and the civil war begins.

title: Somaliland declaration
description: Clan elders and the SNM declare in Burao that the north resumes the independence of 1960; though unrecognised, Somaliland governs itself from then on.

title: US-led intervention
description: US Marines land on Mogadishu's beaches to open the roads for food convoys as famine kills hundreds of thousands.

title: Battle of Mogadishu
description: Two American helicopters are shot down and the rescue battle through the night kills hundreds of Somalis and eighteen US soldiers, scaring the intervention away.

title: Puntland founded
description: Clan conferences in Garowe proclaim the autonomous Puntland State, the first of the federal regional states to form.

title: Transitional Federal Government
description: After two years of talking in Kenya, warlords and civil society elect Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed president of a new transitional government.

title: Islamic Courts take Mogadishu
description: The Islamic Courts Union beats the warlord alliance in the capital and briefly restores order to the city.

title: Ethiopian-backed forces take over
description: The Courts' forces abandon the capital and Ethiopian tanks roll in; their extreme wing, al-Shabaab, begins an insurgency.

title: Famine declared
description: The UN declares famine in two southern regions as drought and al-Shabaab blockages starve the south; a quarter of a million people die.

title: Farmajo elected
description: MPs elect Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed, nicknamed Farmajo, as president of the federal government.

title: Mogadishu bombing
description: A truck bomb at a packed junction kills nearly six hundred people, one of the deadliest terrorist attacks ever recorded.
